title: sutra_dead: Dart false positives — intra-file references to private symbols not resolved
description: On the swe_dashboard workspace (Flutter, 160 files), sutra_dead reports 330 dead symbols and 27 unreachable files, nearly all false positives. Two classes: (1) private Dart symbols (underscore-prefixed methods/consts/classes) referenced only within their own file are reported dead — e.g. widget State helper methods called from build() (_ContextBarState::_openChart, _DatesTabState::_buildResults), private consts used by same-file functions (_monthLengths in calendar.dart), private State classes returned by createState(). Spot-checks during the 2026-07-24 swe_dashboard release review confirmed these are live (a reviewer verified by grep). Suggests the Dart reference extractor misses intra-file/implicit-this call edges. (2) All 27 test/*.dart files are listed as unreachable files — Dart test entry points (main() invoked by the test runner) need the same exemption Rust #[test]/tests/*.rs already get (sutra/13). Impact: the dead list is unusable for Dart workspaces; the release-review skill's pack-build had to caveat it as "do not chase".
execution_record: Added RefContextKind::Read (as_str/from_str) and emit it in dart.rs for private (underscore) identifier value reads, gating out declaration sites with existing is_definition_name plus new is_dart_binding_name (excludes static_final_declaration/initialized_identifier/initialized_variable_definition name child, and formal_parameter/type_parameter/label/declared_identifier/constructor_signature wholesale). Scoped to private/underscore names deliberately — matches the bug (intra-file private) and keeps blast radius minimal; cross-file public tear-offs are out of scope. Read is kind-agnostic in the resolver (not in the use_kind_filter set) and maps to EdgeKind::Reference (weight 0.2) via the existing `_ =>` fallback, so no resolver/graph code changed. Added test/ + integration_test/ + %_test.dart exclusions to find_unreachable_files SQL. Investigation surprises: (a) createState `_ContextBarState()` classifies as Call and fails kind_compatible(Call,class), but resolves anyway via the existing unfiltered fallback branch (fallback len==1) — so NO change to kind_compatible was needed; verified relaxing it would have broken test_kind_aware_call_prefers_function. (b) The live DB showed `_ContextBarState` with an empty unresolved_name (stale/older MCP binary); the current parser extracts the name correctly. Verified end-to-end with a throwaway pipeline integration test against the real swe_dashboard workspace: 330→2 dead symbols, 27→6 unreachable files (remaining 6 are genuine third_party/*_web.dart conditional-import platform variants + a build hook), all three named symbols now live. Full suite: 39 suites / 783 tests pass; clippy clean on changed files. Pre-existing unrelated Cargo.toml edit (indexing_slicing lint) left unstaged.
reproduction: sutra_workspace(path=/home/josh/nhs/soft/astrology/swe_dashboard, enable=["analysis"]); sutra_dead(workspace="swe_dashboard") -> 330 dead symbols, 27 unreachable files. Counter-example: lib/core/calendar.dart _monthLengths is referenced by daysInMonth in the same file but listed dead.
root_cause: Two independent mechanisms. (1) The Dart reference extractor (walk_refs_recursive/classify_ref_context) only emitted refs for Call/Construction/TypeUse/FieldAccess/Import contexts and dropped everything classified `Other`, which includes bare value reads: const/variable reads (`_monthLengths[i]` → index_expression) and method/function tear-offs (`onPressed: _openChart` → named_argument). Private same-file symbols referenced only as values therefore had zero inbound resolved refs and read as dead. (2) find_unreachable_files excluded only Rust `tests/`; Dart tests live under `test/`/`integration_test/`, so all test files (fan_in_files=0, main() invoked by the runner) were flagged unreachable. Dead *symbols* in test files were already exempt via FLAG_CFG_TEST (flags & 7 filter), so only the file-level path exclusion was missing.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Review (vidhi-review, codex + claude verification of e3ded9b): REQUEST CHANGES — two confirmed bugs in landed code.

[HIGH] is_dart_binding_name misses the `identifier_list` declaration form → private-symbol self-reference masks genuine dead code. Empirically verified (parse of `external static var _dead;`): the declaration identifier itself emits a RefContextKind::Read (line/col at the declaration), which the kind-agnostic resolver binds back to the same symbol, giving it a self-inbound-ref and hiding it from find_dead_symbols. This is the inverse of the bug the commit fixes (false negative). Note: `int _count;` and multi-var `int _a, _b;` ARE handled correctly (declared_identifier / initialized_identifier) — the gap is specific to the bare `identifier_list` form used by external/static var without initializer. Catch-clause (`catch (_err)`) and for-in (`for (var _x ...)`) bindings ALSO emit self-Reads but are not indexed as dead-checkable symbols, so those are harmless noise rather than masking. Fix: recognize `identifier_list` children as binding names (prefer a field-name / declaration-container check over the immediate-parent allowlist); add regression test for a private `external static var _dead;` producing zero Read refs at its declaration.

[MEDIUM] find_unreachable_files LIKE patterns treat `_` as a wildcard (src/db/mod.rs:1286-1288). Verified in sqlite: `'latest.dart' LIKE '%_test.dart'` and `'contest.dart' LIKE '%_test.dart'` both return 1 — production Dart files ending in "…test.dart" are wrongly excluded from unreachable-file reporting. Same unescaped-underscore issue on the `integration_test` segment patterns. Fix: add `ESCAPE '\'` and escape the literal underscores (verified `'%\_test.dart' ESCAPE '\'` returns 0 for latest.dart), or switch to GLOB. Add tests: foo_test.dart excluded; latest.dart/contest.dart still reported.

Structural: sutra_review risk 0.963 but that is inherent file churn/blast-radius (db/mod.rs, parser/dart.rs hotspots), not this 68-line additive change. The Read→Reference weak-edge mapping and kind-agnostic resolver handling of Read were verified correct. Filing follow-up bug task.
